title: MITIGATING SOCIAL SYCOPHANCY VIA PLURALISTIC PREFERENCE OPTIMIZATION
reasoning: The paper focuses on mitigating 'social sycophancy' in LLMs—a behavior where models overly affirm users, even when the user describes harmful intent or asks for advice in interpersonal conflicts. By evaluating on datasets like r/AmITheAsshole (AITA) and Problematic Action Statements (PAS), and employing 'pluralistic alignment' to model multi-stakeholder perspectives, the paper benchmarks and proposes methods for handling moral judgments and ethical dilemmas in AI.
